verified: edh-d-74 review (Commander lane pay-or-else, concept round; rank 8783 of the EDHREC top 20,000), by hand against the Oracle text and the rulings of 2006-07-15 and 2008-10-01: Defender and flying are keywords; "Cumulative upkeep--An opponent gains 1 life." is the cumulative upkeep keyword (CR 702.24a) with the cost part opponentGainsLife 1 (the payer chooses an opponent for each age counter, ruling 2006-07-15), read only after a cumulative upkeep's dash (parser/holes/misc.ts#opponentGainsLifeCost)

edh-d-74 review (rank 9495), by hand against the Oracle text and the rulings of 2006-07-15: "Cumulative upkeep--Flip a coin." is the keyword with the cost part flipCoin (one called coin per age counter; the flips are called because the card says win and lose, CR 705.2); "Whenever you win a coin flip, ~ deals 1 damage to any target" is trg coinFlip won:true; "Whenever you lose a coin flip, ~ deals 1 damage to any target of an opponent's choice" is coinFlip won:false with an any target chosen by an opponent (TargetSpec.chooser anOpponent, CR 601.2c, 601.7a: the controller picks which opponent in a multiplayer game)

edh-d-74 review (rank 12929), by hand against the Oracle text and the rulings of 2004-10-04 and 2008-10-01: the keyword's cost is exileTop 1 (the top card of the library; unpayable with too few cards in it); "When a player doesn't pay ~'s cumulative upkeep" is the action event failCumulativeUpkeep of the permanent itself by any player (eff.edhd74.player.exile.allLibrary: that player exiles every card of their library, the event's player); the activated ability's cost is the same exileTop part and its effect a prevention shield of the next 1 damage to you this turn (existing templates) (CR 702.24a, 118.12, 608.2f, 603.2; cites from memory, unverified)

edh-d-74 review (rank 19853), by hand against the Oracle text and the ruling of 2006-07-15: the keyword is a plain {1} cumulative upkeep; "Whenever you pay ~'s cumulative upkeep" is the action event payCumulativeUpkeep by you of the permanent itself (emitted by the cumulative upkeep's pay step before the unpaid branch, effects/handlers/pay.ts); the may-search is for a creature card with mana value EQUAL to the number of age counters on ~ (existing template eff.stdrx20.search.desc), put onto the battlefield, then shuffle (CR 702.24a, 118.12, 608.2f, 603.2; cites from memory, unverified)

edh-d-74 review (rank 5975), by hand against the Oracle text and the rulings of 2012-05-01: a forEach over every creature (objects are visited by controller in APNAP order, CR 608.2f, 101.4) in which that creature's controller (not the spell's) may pay X life, else sacrifices that creature (eff.edhd74.forEach.itsController.sacrificesIt.unlessPayLife): sacrificeChoice by the controller of the creature with the creature as the only choice, X the spell's announced X; a player without the life or declining sacrifices; the decisions are made one creature at a time and the payments and sacrifices happen as they go, where the ruling has all decisions first and then everything at once (recorded deviation: decisions are made and carried out one creature at a time, so an earlier sacrifice can change a later one (a control-stealing creature sacrificed first, or a life-total lock such as Platinum Emperion sacrificed first), found by the Opus review and left; the controller of each creature is read as the loop reaches it)

edh-d-74 review (rank 13452), by hand against the Oracle text and the rulings of 2004-10-04: forEach over every creature (fixed when the spell resolves, APNAP), its controller pays {1} else sacrifices a permanent of their choice (sacrificeChoice, filter any permanent, count 1; eff.edhd74.forEach.itsController.sacrificesPermanentOfChoice.unlessPay); the list is fixed at the start, so a creature sacrificed to pay for another is still asked for its own payment (ruling: you can't avoid a payment that way) (CR 702.24a, 118.12, 608.2f, 603.2; cites from memory, unverified)

edh-d-74 review (rank 6395), by hand against the Oracle text and the rulings of 2020-01-24: forEach over every spell and ability the controller's opponents control on the stack (eff.edhd74.forEach.spellAndAbility.opponents.counterItUnlessPay), its controller pays {4} else it is countered; the ruling has all choices first, then everything countered at once (recorded deviation: each is countered as its controller declines, with the same outcome) (CR 702.24a, 118.12, 608.2f, 603.2; cites from memory, unverified)
